title: Haud ignarus malorum miseris succurrere disco,
html_source: Latin for: “not at all ignorant of misfortune, I have learned to succor the miserable.” This would be better uttered by Bloom. Perhaps Joyce’s purpose was to make that contrast, although Stephen does, in fact, attempt to help the man, but Bloom had taken possession of Stephen’s money for safekeeping.
